decks.domain: Obtaining a new Indiana credential: credential types, Real ID, residency, learner's permits, vision and the two exams

cards.front: What three kinds of credentials does the Indiana BMV issue?
cards.back: The Indiana Bureau of Motor Vehicles issues three kinds of credentials: identification cards, learner's permits and driver's licenses.

cards.front: Which credentials fall under the learner's permit category, and which under the license category?
cards.back: The learner's permit category covers the driver, motorcycle and commercial learner's permits, while the license category covers the driver's license and the CDL.

cards.front: Who can get an Indiana identification card at no cost?
cards.back: An identification card costs nothing for a person who is already eighteen or will turn eighteen on or before the next General or Municipal Election.

cards.front: How does a credential for an Indiana resident under twenty-one look different?
cards.back: Credentials for Indiana residents under twenty-one use a vertical layout and print the dates on which the holder turns eighteen and twenty-one.

cards.front: When did Indiana start issuing redesigned credentials, and are older cards still good?
cards.back: Indiana began issuing redesigned credentials with new security features in two thousand nineteen, and older cards remain valid until the expiration date printed on them.

cards.front: What mark shows that an Indiana credential is Real ID-compliant?
cards.back: A star in the upper right corner shows that a credential is Real ID-compliant and can serve as identification for federal purposes.

cards.front: What did the federal Real ID Act of two thousand five set out to do?
cards.back: The federal Real ID Act of two thousand five set minimum standards so that compliant state credentials can be used for federal purposes such as boarding commercial flights or entering military and other secure federal sites.

cards.front: Since when has Indiana met the Real ID Act requirements?
cards.back: Indiana has met the Real ID Act requirements since January one, two thousand ten.

cards.front: Which licenses and ID cards do federal agencies like DHS and TSA accept at their facilities?
cards.back: Federal agencies such as DHS and TSA accept only Real ID-compliant licenses and ID cards for entry to federal facilities, TSA airport checkpoints included.

cards.front: When and how can a non-compliant Indiana credential be upgraded to Real ID?
cards.back: A non-compliant Indiana credential can be upgraded to Real ID during a renewal, amendment or replacement, using original documents or certified copies.

cards.front: What four kinds of documents must you bring to a branch for a Real ID upgrade?
cards.back: For a Real ID upgrade the branch visit must include documents proving identity, lawful status, Social Security number and Indiana residency.

cards.front: Where can you find the full list of Real ID documents?
cards.back: The full Real ID document list is in Appendix A and at REALID.IN.gov, and the BMV toll-free line is eight hundred eighty-eight-six hundred ninety-two-six thousand eight hundred forty-one.

decks.domain: Obtaining a new Indiana credential: credential types, Real ID, residency, learner's permits, vision and the two exams

cards.front: Who can get an Indiana credential, and how can Indiana residency be shown?
cards.back: Only legal Indiana residents can obtain an Indiana credential; residency can be shown by keeping an Indiana home address without claiming another state, by being registered to vote in Indiana, or by having a dependent enrolled in an Indiana elementary or secondary school.

cards.front: Which people are not treated as Indiana residents for credential purposes?
cards.back: For credential purposes, college students and active-duty service members who do not claim Indiana residency, temporary employees and anyone not intending Indiana to be a permanent home are not treated as residents.

cards.front: What happens if the BMV finds you already hold a credential from another state?
cards.back: If the BMV finds that an applicant already holds a credential from another state, territory, DC or Puerto Rico, that card must be surrendered before the Indiana application is processed.

cards.front: How many credentials may an Indiana resident hold at one time?
cards.back: Indiana residents may hold only one credential at a time, even when the other one came from another state, so any other credential is surrendered when applying.

cards.front: How long does a new Indiana resident have to get an Indiana driver's license?
cards.back: A person who becomes an Indiana resident has sixty days to get an Indiana driver's license.

cards.front: What must a new resident who was never licensed in another state do before applying for a license?
cards.back: A new resident who has never held a valid license from another state must hold an Indiana learner's permit for one hundred eighty days before applying for a driver's license.

cards.front: Which new-resident rule uses sixty days and which uses one hundred eighty days?
cards.back: The sixty-day deadline applies to a new resident getting an Indiana license, while the one hundred eighty-day rule applies to holding an Indiana learner's permit when the person was never licensed in another state.

cards.front: What may a new resident aged eighteen or older bring to transfer an out-of-state license?
cards.back: A new resident aged eighteen or older with a valid out-of-state license brings one of three items: that license, a copy of the official driving record, or a verification letter.

cards.front: When does a transferring applicant have to take the knowledge exam?
cards.back: A knowledge exam is required when the out-of-state license expired less than five years ago or has been held unrevoked for less than one year.

cards.front: What tests are needed when the out-of-state license expired more than five years ago?
cards.back: When the out-of-state license has been expired for more than five years, the applicant must pass both a knowledge exam and a driving skills test.

cards.front: How does the testing differ for a license expired under five years versus over five years?
cards.back: An out-of-state license expired for less than five years means a knowledge exam only, while one expired for more than five years means a knowledge exam plus a driving skills test.

cards.front: What must a transferring applicant under eighteen meet and pass?
cards.back: A transferring applicant under eighteen must be older than sixteen years and one hundred eighty days and have held a valid out-of-state license for at least one hundred eighty days, and must also pass a knowledge exam and a vision screening.

decks.module: ID cards, permits and supervised practice
decks.domain: Obtaining a new Indiana credential: credential types, Real ID, residency, learner's permits, vision and the two exams

cards.front: Who may be issued an Indiana identification card?
cards.back: An identification card can be issued to an Indiana resident of any age who does not hold a driver's license.

cards.front: How can an ID card holder become allowed to operate a motor driven cycle?
cards.back: An ID card holder aged at least fifteen who passes an MDC knowledge exam receives an MDC endorsement on the card and may operate a motor driven cycle.

cards.front: How long are an ID card and an MDC endorsement valid?
cards.back: An identification card and an MDC endorsement are valid for six years, but cards for lawful temporary residents expire on the end-of-stay date.

cards.front: What does an applicant aged sixteen or older need to get a learner's permit?
cards.back: An applicant aged sixteen or older gets a learner's permit by proving identity, lawful status, Social Security number and residency with Appendix A documents and passing a vision screening and a knowledge exam.

cards.front: What extra requirements apply to a learner's permit applicant under sixteen?
cards.back: An applicant under sixteen must be at least fifteen and show a Certificate of Driver Education Enrollment from a BMV-licensed behind-the-wheel provider, dated no more than three weeks before the class starts.

cards.front: How do permit requirements differ for applicants sixteen or older and those under sixteen?
cards.back: A learner's permit applicant aged sixteen or older needs documents, a vision screening and a knowledge exam, while one under sixteen must also be at least fifteen and show proof of enrollment in behind-the-wheel training.

cards.front: Does a certificate from an online theory course prove driver education enrollment?
cards.back: The certificate of completion from an online theoretical course is not accepted as proof of driver education enrollment.

cards.front: What must a learner's permit applicant younger than eighteen provide about an emergency contact?
cards.back: A learner's permit applicant younger than eighteen must name an emergency contact who is at least eighteen.

cards.front: How long is an Indiana learner's permit valid?
cards.back: Learner's permits are valid for two years from the issue date, except that permits for lawful temporary residents end on the end-of-stay date.

cards.front: How do the validity periods of an ID card, an MDC endorsement and a learner's permit compare?
cards.back: An identification card and an MDC endorsement both last six years, while a learner's permit lasts two years from issue.

cards.front: What is required to renew a learner's permit that has been expired for more than one hundred eighty days?
cards.back: Renewing a learner's permit that has been expired for more than one hundred eighty days requires retesting.

cards.front: When must the knowledge exam be retaken for a permit, and does valid permit time still count?
cards.back: The knowledge exam is retaken after a permit has been expired for more than one hundred eighty days, and any time spent holding a valid permit still counts toward the one hundred eighty-day holding period.

cards.front: Who may supervise a permit holder under sixteen who is enrolled in driver education?
cards.back: A permit holder under sixteen who is enrolled in driver education may drive with a licensed driver training instructor or a BMV-recognized certified driver rehabilitation specialist sitting in the front passenger seat.

cards.front: Who may supervise practice driving for a permit holder under eighteen?
cards.back: A permit holder under eighteen may practice with a relative by blood, marriage or legal status who is at least twenty-five and holds valid driving privileges, or with a licensed spouse who is at least twenty-one, seated in the front passenger seat.

cards.front: Who may supervise practice driving for a permit holder aged eighteen or older?
cards.back: A permit holder aged eighteen or older may practice only with a validly licensed driver who is at least twenty-five, or with a licensed spouse who is at least twenty-one.

cards.front: How old must a relative supervisor be compared with a spouse supervisor?
cards.back: A relative supervising permit practice must be at least twenty-five, but a spouse supervising permit practice need only be licensed and at least twenty-one.

cards.front: Who may supervise a permit holder under eighteen who is in Department of Child Services care?
cards.back: A permit holder under eighteen who is in the care of the Department of Child Services may practice with a licensed relative aged at least twenty-five or with a licensed driver aged at least twenty-five whom the Department approves.

cards.front: Who else may supervise a permit holder under eighteen who is not in driver education?
cards.back: A permit holder under eighteen who is not in driver education may also drive with a licensed driver training school instructor working for a school, or a BMV-recognized certified driver rehabilitation specialist, in the front passenger seat.

decks.domain: Obtaining a new Indiana credential: credential types, Real ID, residency, learner's permits, vision and the two exams

cards.front: Who must pass a vision screening, and what should drivers with glasses or contacts do?
cards.back: Every permit or license applicant, renewals included, must pass a vision screening unless eligible to renew online, and drivers who wear glasses or contacts should say so and wear them for the screening.

cards.front: What can happen if you fail the vision screening at a branch?
cards.back: Failing the branch vision screening can lead to further evaluation, and Driver Ability may still require more testing even when the customer brings a doctor's letter.

cards.front: What does the knowledge exam draw from, and what must you be able to read?
cards.back: The knowledge exam is a multiple-choice test drawn from Indiana law, defensive driving practices and this manual, and it expects you to read and understand regulatory, warning and traffic signs and signals.

cards.front: Which applicants are required to take the knowledge exam?
cards.back: The knowledge exam is required for permit applicants, new residents whose out-of-state license is expired or who hold a valid out-of-country license, new residents under eighteen with an out-of-state license, and residents whose Indiana license expired more than one hundred eighty days ago.

cards.front: What extra requirement applies to a driver renewing with six or more active points?
cards.back: A driver renewing a license with six or more active points on the Indiana record must also take the knowledge exam.

cards.front: When must active-duty military members, spouses or dependents take the knowledge exam at renewal?
cards.back: Active-duty military members, spouses or dependents whose Indiana license has been expired more than one hundred eighty days and who returned from service outside Indiana more than ninety days before renewal must take the knowledge exam.

cards.front: What timing rules apply to taking and retaking the knowledge exam?
cards.back: To take the computer-based knowledge exam the same day you must arrive at least thirty minutes before the branch closes, and after a failure you must wait until the next business day to retake it.

cards.front: What other knowledge exams does the BMV offer besides the driver's exam?
cards.back: Besides the driver's knowledge exam, the BMV offers knowledge exams for CDL endorsements and for motorcycle, MDC and for-hire operation.

decks.domain: Obtaining a new Indiana credential: credential types, Real ID, residency, learner's permits, vision and the two exams

cards.front: Where can a permit holder take the driving skills exam after finishing a driver training course?
cards.back: A permit holder can take the driving skills exam at a participating BMV-licensed driver training school after finishing a course of thirty hours of theory and six hours behind the wheel, and that result stays valid until the permit expires.

cards.front: Which permit holders may a driver training school give the skills exam to?
cards.back: Driver training schools may give the skills exam to any holder of a valid Indiana learner's permit, whether or not the permit carries driver's education restriction J.

cards.front: When must a student take the skills exam at a BMV branch instead of a school?
cards.back: The skills exam must be taken at a BMV branch instead if the student fails either part of the driver education course or the school does not take part in the skills test program.

cards.front: Which new residents must take the skills exam with a BMV examiner?
cards.back: A BMV examiner must give the skills exam to new residents under eighteen who held an unrevoked out-of-state license for at least one hundred eighty days but less than one year, and to new residents holding an out-of-country license.

cards.front: What other situations require a BMV skills exam?
cards.back: A BMV skills exam is also required when an Indiana license has been expired more than five years, when a BMV restriction requires testing, or when a medical complaint or the medical board leads the BMV to require an evaluation.

cards.front: How far ahead can a BMV skills exam be booked, and who supplies the vehicle?
cards.back: A BMV driving skills exam can be booked no more than three weeks and no less than forty-eight business hours in advance, the applicant supplies the vehicle, and the BMV charges nothing for it.

cards.front: Who may ride in the vehicle during the driving skills exam?
cards.back: Only the BMV examiner or other authorized BMV staff may ride in the vehicle during the driving skills exam.

cards.front: Which cameras must be switched off during the skills exam?
cards.back: Interior cameras must be switched off for the whole skills exam, though backup cameras are allowed.

cards.front: What must be true of the vehicle used for the skills exam?
cards.back: The test vehicle must be legally equipped, insured, safe and clean, and its current registration must be shown before the exam.

cards.front: What problems can lead the examiner to reject a test vehicle?
cards.back: The examiner may reject a vehicle, for example one that is not properly registered or has unsafe tires, a missing bumper, broken glass or mirrors, or a door that does not work.

cards.front: What does the examiner do during the driving skills exam?
cards.back: The examiner does not teach during the exam but scores the drive objectively on a standardized form, after asking a few required questions.

cards.front: What driving behaviors does the skills exam score?
cards.back: Skills exam scoring covers lane use and signaling, a safe gap to the vehicle ahead, holding speed and leaving room when being passed, speed control, defensive habits, following instructions and approaching intersections with a full stop when required.

recap_hooks.text: Indiana issues ID cards, permits and licenses; a star marks a Real ID card, and federal sites accept only Real ID.
Upgrade to Real ID at a renewal, amendment or replacement with documents for identity, lawful status, Social Security number and residency.
New residents get an Indiana license within sixty days and keep only one credential.
Never licensed elsewhere means a permit held one hundred eighty days; expired over five years means both tests.

recaps.module: ID cards, permits and supervised practice

recap_hooks.text: At sixteen you need documents, vision and a knowledge exam; under sixteen you also need enrollment proof.
A permit lasts two years; practice with a licensed relative aged twenty-five or more, or a licensed spouse aged twenty-one or more.
Everyone screens their vision, wearing glasses or contacts if they use them.
Arrive at least thirty minutes before closing for a same-day knowledge exam, and retake it the next business day.
Book a BMV skills exam three weeks to forty-eight business hours ahead and bring a legal, insured, safe car.
Only the examiner rides along, interior cameras stay off, and the drive is scored on a standard form.
